variants.direction: L08 DESIGN: Keep a narrow cylindrical neck behind the three original collars, widening into two solid bevel-free angular shoulders. Below the central cargo roof, cut each flank inward as one broad trapezoidal recessed field, then extend the lower side into a clean swept wing-root saddle. Distinguish this fixed saddle from the three moving fan leaves underneath it. Give the exposed leaf tips a straight clipped diagonal, creating a staggered angular fan contour. The largest leaf carries a modest native-style equipment pad. At the rear, side shells terminate ahead of the engine rims so the two separate unequal engines and their short solid mounts remain visible. A broad almost straight transverse spoiler sits above them on two short integral supports with clear air beneath; its ends turn down like the source. Keep the spoiler thin and wide, not a roof box. Pirate character: one repaired shoulder panel, one replaced wing leaf, and abrupt but coherent cut-in flank geometry. Body remains close in scale and fullness to the source. Label L08.
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Make a carefully designed production concept sheet for a PIRATE REFIT OF THE LIBERTY ELITE FIGHTER FROM FREELANCER. This is a specific redesign of the attached ship, recognizably the same family and scale. Simple geometry of individual parts, interesting assembly of distinct functional parts. Keep the original overall proportions: deployed span nearly ship length, substantial original hull depth.

REFERENCE ROLES, in input order:
1. Immutable ORIGINAL COCKPIT, multiple views: reproduce the elongated rounded glazed capsule and its original shell, thin frame boundaries, large curved side panes, long top pane, small rear quarter panes and rounded glass nose. The cabin itself forms the nose. Do not design a new canopy or put a beak ahead of it. Preserve cabin size relative to the ship. The three thin transverse neck flanges behind it are also characteristic.
2. Actual ORIGINAL COMPONENT ASSEMBLY, four views. Grey hull, pink SEPARATE TRANSVERSE REAR SPOILER, blue upper engine, teal lower engine, three different colored articulated wing leaves on EACH SIDE. These colors are explanatory only; do not copy the rainbow palette.
3. Actual motion: the SAME three overlapping rigid leaves on each side fan outward for flight and rotate backward to nest close along the hull for docking. Preserve the three-leaf fan architecture. Study how whole leaves overlap, rather than drawing seams on one fixed triangular wing.
4. Actual rear components: broad raised spoiler with downturned ends and visible air below, upper engine wider and short, lower engine narrower and projecting farther aft. Two distinct engine units on a VERTICAL CENTERLINE. Retain them as individually readable volumes with visible solid attachments.
5. Actual upper cargo hatch. TWO LONG NARROW DOORS SIDE BY SIDE along the roof, seam from nose to tail. They open sideways/up on their outer long edges. Keep a clear central cargo roof with no structure crossing the opening.

DESIGN: reinterpret the connecting hull, wing root shoulders, leaf outlines and spoiler contour. Keep the original's articulated silhouette and readable depth changes. The hull should have a neck, central roof and shaped flanks, changing sections into a designed stern. Give each of the three wing leaves its own solid thickness, overlapping root and short visible hinge housing. They are broad angular plates of different outlines, not six tiny fingers. Preserve the generous deployed fan and full depth. A few deep recesses, recessed service panels, short structural mounts and replacement sheet-metal sections communicate the rough pirate rebuild. Medium detail concentrated around functional joints, calm large hull planes. Liberty streamline/Art Deco character comes from the capsule, collars, fan and proportion, not added architecture. Preserve the separate rear spoiler and the two independent engines. No skeletal rods, exposed pipes, ornamental ribs, stacked armor borders, dorsal towers, skulls, spikes or gothic styling.

PRESENTATION: clean industrial game concept rendering, crisp faceted planes, restrained steel-grey and warm off-white hull with small weathered oxide-red replacement panels, blue-grey original glazing. Sparse wear; no heavy surface noise. Light warm-grey background, soft even studio light, strong readable silhouette, no environment or weapons obscuring the assembly.
Landscape sheet, one consistent design in every view:
- LARGE MAIN VIEW occupying the upper left/center: mostly SIDE THREE-QUARTER, nose LEFT, gently elevated camera, long lens. Show the full cabin, hull height, fan attachments and independent spoiler; minimal foreshortening. Use image 2 upper-left viewing angle.
- Smaller true SIDE elevation below, nose LEFT, wings deployed.
- True TOP at right, nose UP, wings fully deployed. Hatch seam is vertical in this view.
- Two small separate study insets: REAR THREE-QUARTER showing both vertically stacked engines and the spoiler gap; TOP STOWED showing the SAME wing leaves rotated backward and overlapping near the body, not shrunk or removed. Keep body and spoiler unchanged between poses.
Leave space between views. Labels only: concept code, SIDE, TOP, REAR, STOWED. This is a refined concept drawing, not a featureless primitive blockout.

L08 DESIGN: Keep a narrow cylindrical neck behind the three original collars, widening into two solid bevel-free angular shoulders. Below the central cargo roof, cut each flank inward as one broad trapezoidal recessed field, then extend the lower side into a clean swept wing-root saddle. Distinguish this fixed saddle from the three moving fan leaves underneath it. Give the exposed leaf tips a straight clipped diagonal, creating a staggered angular fan contour. The largest leaf carries a modest native-style equipment pad. At the rear, side shells terminate ahead of the engine rims so the two separate unequal engines and their short solid mounts remain visible. A broad almost straight transverse spoiler sits above them on two short integral supports with clear air beneath; its ends turn down like the source. Keep the spoiler thin and wide, not a roof box. Pirate character: one repaired shoulder panel, one replaced wing leaf, and abrupt but coherent cut-in flank geometry. Body remains close in scale and fullness to the source. Label L08.

variants.direction: L09 DESIGN: A different but equally source-faithful refit. Behind the unchanged cabin and three thin collars, make the upper cargo plateau a clean tapered elongated hexagon, carried by a deep belly with a rising rear cut. Flanks have a single broad concave-in-section cut, connecting a compact front wing-root knuckle to the rear shoulder. Keep the central body full-height. Three overlapping fan leaves on each side retain strong pointed angular tips, with one broad inward cut at the root of the foremost visible leaf; coherent substantial plates, not bat wings. The stern side shells end in a paired angular fork embracing the upper engine's SHORT wide collar, leaving the smaller LONG lower engine visibly exposed below and aft. These are solid compact attachment cheeks, not an external cage. Above the pair, an independent transverse spoiler is swept slightly back in plan, with one shallow central kink and downturned ends, clear space under the span. It remains one broad simple airfoil plate, not a split crest. The hull/engine junction and spoiler are the distinguishing silhouette; do not merely repaint L08. Restrained mismatched steel and oxide panels show pirate repairs. Label L09.
